metadata.title: Bridging the Pixel Gap in Browser Automation.
metadata.purpose: Answer one real question in the Plain register: how do you turn the coordinates Claude reports after looking at a screenshot into a click that lands on your real screen? Lands the carry-out that Claude's coordinates live in a resized copy of your screen, and the ratio multiply is what maps them back.
metadata.anchor_pair: B02 -> B04 (screenshot click at 728,409 on a 1456x819 image, scaled by the viewport/1456,819 ratio to land at 1280,720 on a real 2560x1440 screen)

beats.narration_text: Someone assumes Claude's click coordinates land on your screen's exact pixels. They don't — they're scaled from a resized copy of your screenshot. So how do you turn Claude's numbers into a real screen coordinate?

shot.new_visual_element: Writer types 'Claude's click coordinates are my screen's exact pixels, right?', hesitates on 'exact', corrects to 'scaled', lands the real question

beats.narration_text: The browser tool screenshots your screen and sends it to Claude, but Claude's vision encoder resizes every 16:9 image to exactly 1456 by 819 before it looks at anything. The natural guess is that the coordinates Claude reports back are already in your screen's pixels. Click there, and you miss the button.

shot.new_visual_element: A small screenshot rectangle and a larger real-screen rectangle; a dot maps straight across at the same raw numbers and misses

production_viz.label: Same raw pixel, wrong screen
production_viz.mechanic: Left: a small outlined rectangle labelled '1456 × 819 — what Claude sees' on cream, with a terracotta dot inside it and a target ring nearby. Right: a larger outlined rectangle labelled 'YOUR REAL SCREEN', proportioned differently. An arrow carries the dot's raw (x,y) straight across; on the right rectangle the dot lands away from the target ring, marked with a cross.

beats.narration_text: Here's the concrete case. Claude's screenshot is 1456 by 819, and it reports a click at 728, 409 — dead center of that image. Your real viewport is 2560 by 1440. Click at that same pixel on your actual screen, and you land near the top-left corner, nowhere close to the button.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR - screenshot rect labelled 1456x819 with a dot at (728,409); the same raw pixel plotted on the larger 2560x1440 rect lands near the corner, marked with a miss

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR - 728,409 on the wrong canvas
production_viz.mechanic: THE ANCHOR. Left rectangle labelled '1456 × 819' with a terracotta dot at dead center, captioned '(728, 409)'. Right rectangle labelled '2560 × 1440' (visibly larger, same aspect). The exact same (728, 409) coordinate is plotted on the right rectangle, landing near its top-left corner with a cross mark, far from a target ring near center. THIS EXACT PAIR OF RECTANGLES RETURNS AT B04.

beats.narration_text: The fix is the inverse of the resize ratio. Multiply Claude's x by your viewport width over 1456, and its y by your viewport height over 819. Clamp both to the screen's edges so you never click off-screen. That's the whole trick — coordinate_scaling.py does it in twenty lines.

shot.new_visual_element: Formula card: real_x = x * (viewport_w / 1456), real_y = y * (viewport_h / 819), then a clamp note

production_viz.label: The inverse ratio
production_viz.mechanic: Two formula lines build in ink mono on cream: 'real_x = x × (viewport_w / 1456)' then 'real_y = y × (viewport_h / 819)'. Beneath, a smaller line in terracotta: 'clamp to [0, viewport_w-1] / [0, viewport_h-1]'. A small caption bottom-right: 'coordinate_scaling.py — 20 lines'.

beats.narration_text: Back to the anchor: 2560 over 1456 is about 1.76, and so is 1440 over 819 — because both are 16:9. Multiply 728 and 409 by that ratio and you land at 1280, 720, dead center of the real screen. But that single ratio only works because the viewport is 16:9 like the screenshot. A different aspect ratio needs a different lookup table, not this one multiply.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR RETURNS - same two rectangles; the scaled dot now lands on the target; a mismatched-aspect rectangle beside it is struck through

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR RETURNS - scaled, and lands
production_viz.mechanic: THE B02 RECTANGLE PAIR RETURNS, identical. This time the (728, 409) dot is carried across with the ratio applied, landing exactly on the target ring at '(1280, 720)' inside the 2560×1440 rectangle, marked with a check. Off to the side, a third, differently-proportioned rectangle (not 16:9) appears with a dashed outline and a strike-through, captioned 'different lookup table' in ink — the caveat, not the main case.

beats.narration_text: Claude's coordinates live in a resized copy of your screen — multiply by the ratio back to real pixels, or the click lands nowhere near the button.
